items.title: From hidden notes to AI glasses, cheating takes new forms
items.title_zh: 从隐藏笔记到人工智能眼镜，作弊以新的形式出现
items.summary: Cheating on exams is hardly new in Korea. What has changed is the technology used to get away with it, from altered answer sheets and text messages to artificial intelligence (AI)-powered glasses. As the methods grow more sophisticated, detecting them has become increasingly difficult. Even the civil service examinations of the 1392-1910 Joseon Dynasty were vulnerable to cheaters. In a 1699 scandal, 15 of 33 successful candidates were found to have passed through irregular means, including the swapping of names attached to exam papers. Centuries later, mobile phones made cheating a coordinated operation. During the 2004 college entrance exam, students in Gwangju divided up roles among high-scoring test takers, intermediaries and recipients, passing answers through text messages. According to Ministry of Education figures released in 2005, the scores of 472 students were invalidated for cheating on college entrance exams from the 2002 through 2005 academic years. items.title: Cliffs, quarries and memories of a deposed queen
items.title_zh: 悬崖、采石场和被废黜女王的回忆
items.summary: Climb the hill along the city wall north of Dongdaemun Gate and look east. On the far side of the valley, you'll notice houses clustered around a crescent-shaped cliff. If you venture into the valley beyond it, you'll find more of these oddly curved, stark granite cliffs jutting out of the hillsides. These are not geological formations, but remnants of a time when the hills were used as quarries. The quarrying of granite first began during the reconstruction of Gyeongbok Palace in the 1860s and continued through the colonial period, when the stone was used in the construction of iconic buildings such as the Bank of Korea, Seoul Station and the former Government-General Building that stood on the present site of Gwanghwamun. While at least one known temple in the area features a cave-like grotto dug into a natural cliff face, another, Beopwang Temple, has a worship space inside a tunnel bored into the hillside, almost certainly built by the Japanese during World War II. The Invictus Games is an international multisport event for service members and veterans who were wounded, injured or became ill during military service. Britain’s Prince Harry founded it in 2014 to promote the rehabilitation of injured service members and their return to civilian life. The Korea Disabled Veterans Organization announced the team after reviewing applications in September. The five selected are two members of the center’s peer support group, a former head of operations at the center and two current staff members. All were injured while serving in the military and have since rebuilt their lives through rehabilitation and sports. items.title: Korea warns of rare vision-loss risk linked to GLP-1 drugs

items.summary: The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety issued a safety alert Wednesday to medical professionals and patients over a potential risk of a rare eye condition associated with GLP-1 obesity drugs, including popular obesity treatments Wegovy and Mounjaro. The move follows safety measures by overseas regulators concerning nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a condition caused by reduced blood flow to the optic nerve that can lead to sudden, potentially permanent vision loss. In June last year, the European Medicines Agency classified it as a very rare side effect of semaglutide, the active ingredient in Wegovy, estimating it may affect up to 1 in 10,000 users. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration asked drugmakers Monday to add a possible increased risk of NAION to the warnings and precautions on GLP-1 drug labels. The letter advises medical professionals to stop treatment and have patients examined immediately if NAION is suspected in those taking GLP-1 drugs, which aid weight loss by mimicking a hormone that regulates appetite and blood sugar. The president made the remarks in a post on X, formerly Twitter, on the 31st Day of Farmers, reiterating his pledge to take farmers' interests into account when deciding to join the Indo-Pacific trade bloc. "On important issues, including farmland reform ... and the CPTPP, the government will work toward faithfully reflecting voices from the (agricultural) field so as to be helpful to farmers," Lee wrote in the post. The president has previously said that Korea's entry into the CPTPP would be "unavoidable," but has pledged to focus on finding complementary measures to implement when seeking CPTPP membership. While CPTPP membership is expected to help boost Korea's overall exports, the agricultural and fisheries sectors are likely to take a hit from market opening due to imports of cheaper products. items.summary: National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik on Wednesday reaffirmed his commitment to pushing for a constitutional revision, rejecting opposition claims that the revision would be aimed at allowing President Lee Jae Myung to seek a second term. Cho's remarks came as opposition lawmakers have questioned whether he had left open the possibility of Lee seeking another term after he told a press conference in July that an incumbent president's eligibility to seek another term would be up to the people to decide. "As stipulated in Article 128 of the Constitution, the extension of a sitting president's term is not a subject of discussions for a constitutional revision," Cho said during a discussion hosted by the Kwanhun Club, a senior journalists' association. "This should no longer be used for political conflict." Cho said the National Assembly should take the lead in pursuing constitutional reform, adding he plans to launch an advisory committee under his office soon to set the direction and key priorities for the revision. items.title: Rail workers threaten indefinite strike from Dec. 10
items.title_zh: 铁路工人威胁从12月10日起无限期罢工
items.summary: Unionized workers of Korea Railroad Corp. (KORAIL) said Wednesday they will launch an indefinite general strike at 9 a.m. on Dec. 10, demanding improvements to the promotion system and the employment of more safety-related personnel. The Korean Railway Workers' Union announced the plan in a news conference at Seoul Station, warning the walkout will proceed unless its demands are met. In a statement, the union criticized the current promotion system for "unfairly" excluding field workers and said staff shortages in railway operations are directly compromising safety. The union plans to hold a large-scale rally at Seoul Station on Saturday, followed by a two-week safe-operation campaign and a series of regional nighttime rallies beginning Nov. 23. The walkout could disrupt KTX and conventional train services nationwide, as well as subway services in the capital area. Its impact could be greater than that of previous strikes following the integration of high-speed rail operator SR Co. into KORAIL in September.

items.title: Saudi Arabia calls for immediate end to all threats to maritime navigation
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯呼吁立即停止对海上航行的所有威胁
items.summary: RIYADH — The Saudi Council of Ministers has called for an immediate cessation of all acts that threaten the safety of maritime navigation and undermine the security of vital waterways, particularly the Red Sea, the Bab Al-Mandab Strait, and the Strait of Hormuz. The Cabinet reiterated this position during its session chaired by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on Tuesday. In its review of regional and international developments, the Cabinet reaffirmed the Kingdom’s unwavering commitment to supporting all efforts aimed at strengthening regional and global security and stability, while confronting terrorism and dismantling its criminal militias. At the outset of the session, the Crown Prince briefed the Cabinet on the outcomes of his talks with King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa of Bahrain and Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa. He also briefed the Cabinet on the message he received from President Dr. Julius Maada Bio of Sierra Leone and on his phone calls with Prime Minister of Canada Mark Carney and Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic Kyriakos Mitsotakis. The consultations and talks covered Saudi Arabia’s bilateral relations with their countries and ways to further strengthen them, and underscored the importance of continued coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest.In a statement to the Saudi Press Agency following the session, Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary said the Cabinet welcomed the signing of the General Agreement on the GCC Railway Project to connect the member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The Cabinet also commended ongoing efforts to advance strategic cooperation and economic and development integration and to continue implementing King Salman’s vision for strengthening joint GCC action, achieving shared objectives, and meeting the aspirations of the peoples of the GCC countries.On domestic affairs, the Cabinet commended the address of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman at the opening of the sixth Hajj Conference and Exhibition. The address highlighted Saudi Arabia’s efforts to serve the Two Holy Mosques and pilgrims and its continued commitment to improving Hajj services by adopting the latest technologies and strengthening coordination among government agencies. It also highlighted the expansion of the Direct Hajj Program to serve 133 countries and the announcement of new agreements and partnerships to make pilgrims’ journeys easier from their departure from their home countries until their return.The Cabinet reviewed the overall performance of national sectors and systems in implementing strategies, programs, projects, and initiatives, and the progress achieved in development and prosperity indicators. It commended government entities on winning dozens of international and regional awards across various fields, including health, infrastructure, digital government, and technological innovation, reflecting the state’s support and its commitment to providing these and other entities with every enabler to sustain leadership and excellence and achieve the targets of Saudi Vision 2030.The Cabinet approved the Consumer Protection Law. It approved a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the Saudi Ministry of Energy and the Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources for cooperation in the field of petroleum and gas, and another draft MoU in the field of Islamic affairs between the Saudi Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Call and Guidance and the Islamic Community of Burundi, and authorized the minister of Islamic affairs, call and guidance or his deputy to sign it. The Council endorsed an agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Portuguese Republic on the mutual exemption from entry visas for holders of diplomatic and special passports.The Cabinet authorized the minister of communications and information technology or his deputy to discuss and sign with the Jordanian and Syrian sides a draft cooperation agreement in the field of communications and digital infrastructure between the Saudi Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, the Jordanian Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and the Syrian Ministry of Communications and Information Technology.The Council authorized the minister of human resources and social development or his deputy to discuss and sign with the Jordanian side a draft MoU for cooperation in developing workforce skills in the labor market between the Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development and the Accreditation and Quality Assurance Commission of Jordan, and authorized the minister of investment or his deputy to sign a draft agreement between Saudi Arabia and Bangladesh on the reciprocal promotion and protection of investments.The Cabinet also authorized the minister of transport and logistic services, chairman of the board of directors of the Transport General Authority or his deputy to discuss and sign with the Cypriot side a draft MoU between the Saudi Transport General Authority and the Cypriot Deputy Ministry of Shipping for cooperation in maritime affairs.It approved a MoU for cooperation in the field of railways between the Saudi Transport General Authority and the Turkish Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure. The Council authorized the president of the Human Rights Commission or a deputy to discuss and sign with the Digital Cooperation Organization a draft MoU between the Saudi Human Rights Commission and the Digital Cooperation Organization for technical cooperation.The Cabinet has decided that the state shall bear the customs duties stipulated in the Common Customs Law of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states and the value-added tax imposed on the import of a vehicle by a student pursuing studies abroad on a government scholarship, a government employee performing official duties abroad, or any adult family member accompanying either of them abroad. They shall also be exempt from the financial fee imposed on vehicle imports, in accordance with regulations established by the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority.

items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa of Bahrain in Riyadh on Tuesday.During their meeting, the leaders reviewed the historical relations between the two countries, areas of bilateral cooperation, and ways to strengthen and develop them. They discussed the latest regional developments and efforts to enhance security and stability in the region. King Hamad commended the efforts of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the Crown Prince to strengthen relations between the two countries, praising the Kingdom's honorable, historic, and fraternal stances toward Bahrain and its people on various occasions and its support for Bahrain at all levels. He also expressed appreciation for the Saudi leadership's efforts to advance joint Gulf action and its pivotal role in laying the foundations of security, peace, and stability in the region.The Crown Prince affirmed the Kingdom's commitment to strengthening its close, fraternal ties with Bahrain in all sectors, and wished Bahrain and its people continued development and progress. At the outset of the meeting, the Crown Prince welcomed the king of Bahrain to the Kingdom, and the king thanked him for the warm reception and generous hospitality. The Crown Prince conveyed the greetings of King Salman to the king of Bahrain, who reciprocally conveyed his greetings to King Salman.The meeting was attended by Emir of Riyadh Prince Faisal bin Bandar; Minister of State and Member of the Cabinet Prince Turki bin Mohammed bin Fahd; Minister of Sport Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al-Faisal; Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif; Minister of National Guard Prince Abdullah bin Bandar; Minister of State, Member of the Cabinet, and National Security Advisor Dr. Musaed Al-Aiban; Minister of Finance Mohammed Al-Jadaan; Minister of Transport and Logistics Saleh Al-Jasser; and Saudi Ambassador to Bahrain Naif bin Bandar Al-Sudairi.From the Bahraini side, the meeting was attended by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa; Minister of the Royal Court Sheikh Khalid bin Ahmed bin Salman Al Khalifa; Adviser to the King for Media Affairs Nabeel bin Yaaqob Al-Hamar; Adviser to the King for Diplomatic Affairs Sheikh Khalid bin Ahmed bin Mohammed Al Khalifa; Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Minister of Finance and National Economy Sheikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa; Minister of Transportation and Telecommunications Dr. Sheikh Abdulla bin Ahmed Al Khalifa; Chief of Staff of the Bahrain Defense Force Lt. Gen. Theyab bin Saqr Al Nuaimi; and Bahraini Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Sheikh Ali bin Abdulrahman Al Khalifa. Earlier, the Crown Prince received King Hamad at King Khalid International Airport.

items.title: Erdoğan witnesses Saudi-Turkish deal to develop 5,000mg renewable energy projects in Turkiye
items.title_zh: 埃尔多安见证沙特-土耳其在土耳其开发5000毫克可再生能源项目
items.summary: ANTALYA — Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding on cooperation in electricity projects between Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, following his meeting with Saudi Minister of Energy and Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman in Antalya on Tuesday. **media[2792871]** The Memorandum of Understanding was signed by Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, on behalf of Saudi Arabia, and Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar, on behalf of Türkiye. Prince Abdulaziz arrived in Turkiye to attend the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), which began in Antalya on Monday, and will conclude on Nov. 20. Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar stated that the new agreement marks a step forward in advancing the second phase of renewable energy projects being implemented by Saudi company ACWA Power in Turkiye, within the framework of government cooperation between the two countries.In a post on his social media account, the minister explained that the government agreement, signed by the two countries in Riyadh on February 3 and entering into force on October 21, establishes a framework for developing renewable energy projects with a total capacity of 5,000 megawatts in Turkiye, to be implemented by ACWA Power in two phases. **media[2792872]**Bayraktar noted that work is progressing on the first phase, which involves solar energy projects with a combined capacity of 2,000 megawatts in the provinces of Sivas and Karaman, expressing his satisfaction with the progress achieved in implementing these projects.The minister said that the signing of the new memorandum of understanding in Antalya will strengthen efforts to bring the targeted additional capacity of 3,000 megawatts under the second phase into operation. According to the minister, this phase includes the development of wind power plants, supported by high-voltage direct current (HVDC) electricity transmission infrastructure, as well as battery energy storage systems.Bayraktar emphasized that these investments will not only expand Turkey's renewable energy capacity but also deepen strategic energy cooperation with Saudi Arabia through projects aimed at enhancing electricity grid infrastructure and increasing its flexibility and capacity to accommodate renewable energy sources.He stated that Turkey will continue to translate confidence in its energy transformation and investment environment into tangible projects, underscoring the importance of Saudi investments in supporting the country's plans to expand its clean energy capacity.

items.title: Saudi, Ukrainian foreign ministers discuss joint efforts for achieving peace
items.title_zh: 沙特和乌克兰外长讨论实现和平的共同努力
items.summary: PARIS — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan met with Ukrainian Minister for Foreign Affairs Andrii Sybiha in Paris on Tuesday. The meeting was held on the sidelines of the Group of Seven (G7) ministerial meeting. During the meeting, the ministers reviewed bilateral relations and ways to further strengthen and develop them across various fields. They discussed joint efforts to achieve peace and exchanged views on key regional and international issues of mutual interest. Following the meeting, the ministers signed a memorandum of understanding between the government of Saudi Arabia and the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine on the mutual exemption from short-stay visa requirements for holders of diplomatic, special, and service passports.

items.title: Saudi-Qatari-E4 meeting discusses regional de-escalation in Paris
items.title_zh: 沙特-卡塔尔-E4会议在巴黎讨论区域降级
items.summary: PARIS — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan attended a ministerial meeting of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the E4 countries—France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom—on Tuesday. The meeting was held on the sidelines of the Group of Seven (G7) ministerial meeting in Paris. The meeting addressed recent developments in the Middle East, including the terrorist Houthi militia’s continued attacks on civilians and civilian objects in Yemen and Saudi Arabia and their implications for regional security. Participants also discussed diplomatic efforts to support mediation between the United States and Iran to de-escalate tensions and contain ongoing regional crises. The ministers underscored the importance of strengthening international coordination to secure regional waterways, keep trade flowing, and maintain global supply chains.

items.title: GCC defense ministers approve launch of Advanced Command for Unified Military Command in Kuwait
items.title_zh: 海湾合作委员会国防部长批准在科威特建立统一军事司令部高级司令部
items.summary: MANAMA — Secretary General of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Jasem Albudaiwi stated that the ministers of defense of the GCC states approved the opening of an Advanced Command for the Unified Military Command in Kuwait and the allotment of appropriate forces to it. This was among the decisions taken by the 23rd session of the GCC Joint Defense Council, held in Manama on Tuesday, under the chairmanship of Bahraini Minister of Defense Affairs Lt. Gen. Abdullah Al Nuaimi, who is also chairman of the current session. Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman and defense ministers of other GCC countries participated in the meeting. Albudaiwi stated that the decision comes within the framework of strengthening joint Gulf military cooperation and implementing the directives issued by the GCC leaders during their extraordinary meeting held in Jeddah last April, thereby enhancing the member states’ ability to confront threats and challenges and safeguard their security, stability, and sovereignty. Albudaiwi commended the level of military cooperation and coordination among GCC member states in confronting Iranian attacks, as well as the efficiency and courage demonstrated by Gulf armed forces in repelling them. He stressed that the security of GCC member states is a shared responsibility and that their concerted military efforts strengthen their ability to protect their territories and resources. The GCC chief condemned the treacherous Iranian attacks that targeted the GCC states and caused damage to numerous civilian objects and infrastructure. He also expressed the strongest condemnation and denunciation of the heinous Houthi militia assaults on Saudi Arabia and its targeting of the holy sites. He stressed that the GCC states stand united alongside Saudi Arabia, in full solidarity with it, and support all measures it takes to defend its security, stability, territorial integrity, and holy sites.He noted that the session’s agenda included several decisions aimed at strengthening joint Gulf military cooperation and enhancing integration among the armed forces of the GCC member states.

items.title: Saudi Crown Prince, Greek Prime Minister discuss strengthening bilateral ties in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特王储与希腊首相讨论在通话中加强双边关系
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman held a phone call with Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis to discuss bilateral relations and ways to strengthen cooperation between the two countries. During the call on Tuesday, the two leaders reviewed relations between Saudi Arabia and Greece. They also discussed ways to enhance and develop joint cooperation across various fields.

items.title: Municipalities ministry warns of SR5,000 fine for selling tobacco to under-18s
items.title_zh: 市政部门警告，向18岁以下儿童出售烟草将被处以5000里亚尔的罚款
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Municipalities and Housing stressed that the sale or provision of tobacco products to anyone under the age of 18 is prohibited, and that the violators face penalties including a maximum fine of SR5,000, mandatory establishment closure, and doubled penalties for repeat offenses.The ministry instructed that establishments must comply with the regulations governing the activity.It indicated that the ban also extends to permitting anyone under 18 to enter shops that specialize in selling tobacco products or areas designated for serving them. It added that the regulations governing tobacco shops allow sellers to request proof that a buyer has reached the legal age.The ministry warned that both violations are considered serious offenses, each carrying a fine of up to SR5,000, depending on the classification of the relevant municipality or local authority. The ministry noted that the establishment may also be closed in accordance with applicable regulations, and that the fine doubles in the event of a repeat violation.Moreover, the ministry said the regulations governing tobacco shops require establishments to display warning signs about the harms of smoking and clearly state that entry and sales are prohibited for those below the legal age. They also prohibit selling individual cigarettes and distributing tobacco products through free promotional offers, gifts, prizes, or samples. Establishments must also comply with the standards approved by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority.The ministry urged establishment owners to comply with the regulations, as well as to ensure that employees are familiar with the rules governing the activity and the penalties for violations, and curb breaches. The ministry also invited them to consult the detailed requirements for selling and serving tobacco products on its website.

items.title: Saudi Defense Minister leads GCC talks in Bahrain to strengthen Gulf defense cooperation
items.title_zh: 沙特国防部长率领海湾合作委员会在巴林举行会谈以加强海湾防务合作
items.summary: MANAMA — Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman led the Kingdom’s delegation at the 23rd session of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Joint Defense Council, where participants discussed strengthening joint Gulf defense cooperation to enhance security and stability across GCC member states and the wider region. Held Tuesday in Bahrain, the meeting was attended by defense ministers from GCC member states and GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi. During the meeting, the participants reviewed several matters of mutual interest and approved a number of decisions and recommendations included on the meeting’s agenda. **media[2792517]** In his address, Prince Khalid praised the meeting’s constructive outcomes and decisions, emphasizing their role in advancing Gulf defense integration and strengthening coordination and readiness to confront various risks and challenges, ensuring the security and stability of GCC member states. Concluding his remarks, Prince Khalid welcomed GCC defense ministers to Saudi Arabia, which will host the next round of joint Gulf military cooperation meetings at all levels. The Saudi delegation also included Chief of the General Staff General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili and Advisor to the Minister of Defense for Intelligence Affairs Hisham bin Abdulaziz bin Saif. **media[2792519]**

items.title: Saudi Energy revenue rises 11.5% to SR87.2 billion in first nine months of 2026
items.title_zh: 沙特能源收入在2026年前九个月增长11.5%至872亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Energy (SE) reported an 11.5 percent year-on-year increase in revenue to SR87.2 billion during the first nine months of 2026, while net profit rose 4.3 percent to SR12.1 billion, according to the company's latest financial results. The company announced that earnings before depreciation, amortization, interest, zakat and taxes (EBITDA) increased by 6.6 percent to SR34.7 billion, supported by strategic investments, an expanding regulated asset base and growing electricity demand. In the third quarter alone, revenue climbed 12.9 percent to SR35 billion, while net profit increased 0.4 percent to SR5.4 billion. SE Chief Executive Officer Khalid Al-Ghamdi said the company continued to meet rising electricity demand while improving power plant availability, grid reliability and operational efficiency. He highlighted that operational battery energy storage capacity reached 22 gigawatt-hours, achieving the company's 2026 target and strengthening the electricity grid's ability to integrate renewable energy sources. The company's regulated asset base expanded by 16.6 percent year-on-year to SR278.8 billion as of September 30, 2026, supported by continued investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure. Adjusted capital expenditure stood at SR59.6 billion during the first nine months of the year, while SE signed financing agreements worth approximately SR64.4 billion through sukuk and various credit facilities. Operationally, peak electricity demand in the Kingdom rose 2.5 percent to 79,045 megawatts, while total generation capacity reached 56.8 gigawatts. Renewable energy capacity connected to the national grid reached approximately 19.3 gigawatts, while SE's transmission network expanded by 6 percent to 110,950 circuit kilometers. The company's customer base reached approximately 11.7 million, with 237,762 new customers connected during the first nine months of 2026, representing a 30 percent year-on-year increase. SE also reported a 16 percent improvement in its System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), which fell to 37.17 minutes per customer. In a subsequent development, the company announced an adjustment to electricity service tariffs effective January 1, 2027, stating that the change is not expected to have a material financial impact on its results under the existing regulatory framework.
